references.text: God opened Hagar's eyes so that she saw the water well – an example of how God can close or open people's eyes according to His will ([ref:Gen 21:19|Genesis 21:19]).
The Lord opened Balaam's eyes so that he saw the angel of the Lord – an Old Testament example of how God controls what people see and do not see ([ref:Num 22:31|Numbers 22:31]).

Elisha prayed for the Lord to open his servant's eyes, and he saw the mountains filled with horses and chariots of fire. This demonstrates God's power to open and close people's spiritual sight ([ref:2 Kgs 6:17|2 Kings 6:17]).

Elisha prayed for the enemy army to be struck with blindness, and later for their eyes to be opened again. God withheld their sight and then restored it, just as He withheld the disciples' ability to recognize Jesus ([ref:2 Kgs 6:18-20|2 Kings 6:18-20]).

Isaiah prophesies about a people who see but do not understand. God's withholding of the disciples' recognition of Jesus parallels this prophecy concerning spiritual blindness ([ref:Isa 6:9-10|Isaiah 6:9-10]).

The prophecy that the eyes of the blind will be opened in the messianic age. In Luke 24:16, there is a temporary withholding of sight that points forward to the revelation in verse 31 ([ref:Isa 35:5|Isaiah 35:5]).

In contrast to verse 16: the disciples' eyes were opened and they recognized Him. Together these verses show that it was God's will that both withheld and then enabled their recognition ([ref:Lk 24:31|Luke 24:31]).
Mary Magdalene saw Jesus but did not recognize Him – a parallel to the disciples on the road to Emmaus, where the risen Jesus was not immediately recognized ([ref:Jn 20:14|John 20:14]).
The disciples did not know that it was Jesus standing on the shore. Another example of how the risen Jesus was not immediately recognized by His own ([ref:Jn 21:4|John 21:4]).

Paul writes that God gave Israel a spirit of stupor, eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear. This is a theological parallel to God actively withholding the disciples' ability to recognize Him ([ref:Rom 11:7-8|Romans 11:7-8]).
